I will do it mostly the way I have done in recent years, then adjust a little by what I saw around me. On 10.5 mu, I cannot fool around too much. If I change too much and the crop fails, that hurts more than wasting a bit of fertilizer. I have well water, so I will lean on that and keep the field from going dry at the key time. For wheat, I will keep the stronger land in it because wheat needs the field kept neat and fed well. After wheat harvest, I will put millet on that same land, because millet fits our place and does not ask as much water as maize. I will put the rest in maize in summer, because maize gives steady grain if I feed it enough and give water at the right time. I only went to primary school, but after 50 years I still count the same way: what did well last year, what the neighbors used, and how much money I can still keep for spray, water, and some hired help if needed. So I will use improved or hybrid seed where I saw good stands before, put enough nitrogen so the crop does not go hungry, keep phosphorus in the base fertilizer, add some potassium though not too much, irrigate wheat more than millet, and spray when insects or disease show up instead of waiting too long.
